name: [Portal] Import medailonky into CRM, match to partners, resolve duplicates (migration)
description:
### Summary

This task is the second half of migrating existing partner profiles (medailonky) into CRM. It takes the normalized dataset produced by the WordPress export and writes it into the new CRM partner tables, so that existing partners find their profile pre-filled when they first log into the Partner Portal and the public websites can switch to the CRM-backed API without losing content. The difficult part is matching: WordPress records have no stable key to a Shoptet partner, the same company can appear on the Czech, Slovak and Hungarian sites, and contact data on the websites may differ from billing data already held in CRM or on the project. The task delivers an idempotent import command with deterministic matching rules, a documented precedence for conflicting fields, a report of ambiguous and unmatched records for manual resolution, a dry-run mode, and integration tests on a fixture dataset. It depends on the partner domain layer and on the export task.

### Why?

The export () produces the dataset; this task puts it into CRM so every existing partner finds their medailonek pre-filled on first login and the websites can switch to the API without losing content. The hard part is not the insert but the matching: WordPress records carry no stable key to a Shoptet partner, the same company may appear on CZ, SK and HU, and WordPress contact data can differ from what CRM or the project already holds for billing. Wiki Q4 assigns these decisions to DevRel at implementation time.

### What?

An idempotent import command that reads the normalized dataset, matches each record to an existing partner (API-partner project, CRM company) by deterministic rules, creates the `st_crm.partner` and `partner_lng` rows, links categories and logos, and writes an unmatched/ambiguous report for manual resolution. Field-precedence rules (Q4) are documented in the package. Dry-run mode; re-running with the same input changes nothing.

### Acceptance Criteria

Matching rules implemented in a documented order: IČO → website domain → contact e-mail → normalized name; every match records which rule fired

A record matched to exactly one existing partner creates one 

partner

 row linked to it; CZ/SK/HU records of the same company collapse into one partner with up to three 

partner_lng

 rows

Ambiguous (several candidates) and unmatched records are not imported; they go to a report with the candidates for manual decision

Field precedence (Q4) documented and applied: public fields from WordPress, identity and billing fields (billing e-mail, IČO, DIČ, company name) from CRM/project; conflicts listed per record

Texts imported per language with a defined status (approved by default so websites keep content) and 

approvedById

 set to a system import user

Dry-run prints the full plan without writing; the real run is idempotent (second run = zero changes)

Integration test on a fixture dataset covers clean match, multi-site merge, ambiguous, unmatched and re-run; PHPStan level 10

### Open questions

- Wiki Q4: the precedence rules above are a proposal for DevRel to confirm. Who resolves the unmatched list (Partnership in CRM?) and by when?
- Import as approved or as draft? Approved keeps the websites populated at cutover; draft forces every partner to re-publish. Proposed: approved.
- WordPress partners with no Shoptet account at all: create partner rows without a project link (claimed later in the portal) or skip?

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- Go through the domain layer from  with an import-safe write path (no portal-user mapping); no raw SQL in the command.
- Candidate match keys: `st_api.partner` (`projectId`, `homepage`; `database/schema/st_api.sql` L120); project billing fields (`ico`, `billEmail`, `billCompany`) written today by `admin/controllers/ApiPartnerController.php:356` via `ProjectSaverHelper`; `st_crm.partner.cin / tin / emailForSync / emailForCommunication`.
- Constraints: `partner.slug` globally UNIQUE; `partner_lng` UNIQUE (partnerId, language, status). Import generates one slug per partner and one row per language and status.
- Symfony Console command in the PartnerPortal package; writes to the shared `st_crm` silo through the standard connection pattern.
- Logos: store under a generated filename, same rule as the edit screen ().
